ads.angle: The last thing your edit needs
ads.headline:
The cut is ready.
Is the voice?
ads.primary_text: A finished edit can still be waiting for the right voice. Compare two reads of the same scene and hear which delivery belongs.
ads.script: Your cut is finished. The voice still feels wrong. Hear one scene with two different reads, then choose the delivery that fits your edit. Start with the comparison.
ads.delivery: Warm, grounded British English creative producer speaking to another editor. Conversational, precise and confident. A small pause after the opening two sentences. Avoid hype and an announcer voice. Read only the supplied script.

ads.headline:
Same scene.
Different feeling.
ads.primary_text: The picture stays the same. So do the words. Change the delivery and hear what happens to the scene.
ads.script: A voice can change the whole scene. Same picture. Same words. Two different reads. Play them side by side and hear what changes. Find the voice your story needs.
ads.delivery: British English. An intimate, thoughtful creative voice, with light rhythmic emphasis on 'Same picture. Same words.' Let the idea build naturally. Calm and inviting rather than promotional. Read only the supplied script.

ads.headline:
Make the first line
worth following.
ads.primary_text: Before a listener commits to the whole story, they hear a voice. Compare two readings of one original passage.
ads.script: One line can pull a reader into a story. Or leave them outside it. Hear the same passage read two ways, then choose the narrator you want to follow.
ads.delivery: British English literary narrator. Warm, articulate and quietly compelling. A brief pause after the second sentence, then invite the listener into the comparison. No grand trailer delivery. Read only the supplied script.

ads.headline:
A whole story
starts with one voice.
ads.primary_text: Start with one scene, not a whole manuscript. Listen to two deliveries and decide which makes you want the next chapter.
ads.script: Before you choose a voice for a whole book, listen to one moment. Compare two readings of an original scene. Which one makes you want the next chapter? Listen, then decide.
ads.delivery: British English. Friendly, assured audiobook producer, speaking directly to an independent author. Natural questions, a little curiosity and a warm invitation at the end. Read only the supplied script.
